subject: Maths
title: 5 times table
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (2, 5, 10 Times Tables) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can recall and use the 5 times table to multiply and divide.

key_vocab.definition: The 5 times table is a list of multiples of 5: numbers we get when we count in 5s. Numbers in the 5 times table always end in 0 or 5.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recall and use the 5 times table to multiply and divide.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: 5 times table -- The 5 times table is a list of multiples of 5: numbers we get when we count in 5s. Numbers in the 5 times table always end in 0 or 5.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiplication is repeated addition. 5 × 4 means ‘4 groups of 5’. You can also think of it as ‘5 groups of 4’ — the answer is the same.
5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 5×4 = 20
Four groups of 5

Key examples:
  ✓ 1 × 5 = 5  (starting point)
  ✓ 2 × 5 = 10  (double)
  ✓ 5 × 5 = 25  (halfway to 10)
  ✗ 3 × 5 = 16  (wrong)
  ✗ 5 × 0 = 5  (any × 0 = 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single multiplication
  Calculate 6 × 5
  6 groups of 5
  5 + 5 + 5 + 5  ...
  = 30
  = 30
  (Skip-count in 5s 6 times to reach 30.)

Example 2 – missing factor
  Solve: ___ × 5 = 20
  How many 5s in 20?
  Count up: 5, 10, 15, ...
  = 4
  = 4
  (Divide: 20 ÷ 5 = 4.)
